hypotheses.mechanism_label: Confined acid-water network with dynamic-freezing crossover
hypotheses.description: Proton transport occurs mainly through a continuous H3PO4/H2O hydrogen-bond network confined within attapulgite fiber channels and inter-fiber voids. Above the crossover, network rearrangement enables VTF-like cooperative hopping; below it, partial freezing/rigidification of the confined liquid raises the apparent barrier and yields a higher-Ea regime.
hypotheses.key_prediction: The breakpoint temperature should track signatures of carrier-medium mobility loss rather than acid loading alone, and high-temperature conductivity should scale more strongly with total liquid content N than with acid/water ratio R.

hypotheses.mechanism_label: Two-population bound-water network with sequential activation
hypotheses.description: The attapulgite hosts two proton-conducting carrier populations: weakly bound acid-water domains that are mobile at higher temperature and strongly bound interfacial water/acid species that dominate after the more labile network becomes dynamically arrested. The observed breakpoint reflects a redistribution between these populations rather than a single homogeneous medium.
hypotheses.key_prediction: Samples with similar N but different proportions of interfacial vs less-bound liquid should show similar room-temperature conductivity yet different breakpoint temperatures and low-temperature activation energies.

hypotheses.mechanism_label: Meyer-Neldel compensated hopping in a heterogeneous confined proton glass
hypotheses.description: Transport is dominated by proton hopping across a distribution of confined hydrogen-bond environments whose local barriers and prefactors are strongly compensation-coupled. The apparent breakpoint emerges from barrier-population reshuffling with temperature, while the underlying physics remains thermally activated but disorder-dominated.
hypotheses.key_prediction: Across samples and temperature segments, pre-exponential factors should continue to co-vary systematically with extracted Ea, and changes in conductivity with composition should be larger than changes in best-fit Ea.

hypotheses.mechanism_label: Interfacial proton shell percolation around attapulgite fibers
hypotheses.description: Most protons move along acid-rich interfacial shells coating attapulgite surfaces rather than through a bulk-like confined liquid core. Increasing N mainly increases shell connectivity and wet inter-fiber bridges, while R has weaker leverage because the dominant pathway is set by surface-mediated proton relays in a hydration-stabilized shell.
hypotheses.key_prediction: Conductivity should be much more sensitive to variables that change interfacial coverage/connectivity than to moderate shifts in acid/water ratio, and any impedance arc should appear only when interfacial pathways become partially disconnected at low liquid loading.

reasoning_notes: These hypotheses compete mainly on whether the conductive medium is a single confined acid-water population or split strong/weak-bound populations, whether transport is predominantly cooperative VTF-like or Arrhenius/Meyer-Neldel compensated hopping, and whether connectivity is a continuous confined liquid network, heterogeneous confined domains, or interfacial core-shell pathways. The strong N-dependence, weak R-dependence, near-universal breakpoint detection, and dominant VTF model preference motivate H1, while the dual-Ea landscape and strong Meyer-Neldel compensation keep H2-H4 viable alternatives.
